Hi Jake — thanks for the numbers, that helps a lot. Based on your mix (mostly short queries, ~10% long notes) here are our high-level recommendations: 

1) Shortlist and rationale (attached PDF has details):
- Candidate A: RedInfer-13B-8k (aggressively quantized) — lowest latency, very good for UI Q&A, cheaper per-token but may show small quality gaps on nuanced clinical summarization.
- Candidate B: RedInfer-70B-8k (bfloat/quant mix) — higher quality on summarization and long-context concatenation; higher cost and memory.
- Candidate C: RedInfer-13B-32k-window (sharded) — middle ground if you expect mobiing many long docs frequently; better for long-note extraction at lower cost than 70B but needs more complex routing.

2) Sizing back-of-envelope (for Dedicated pool):
- Baseline: 10 rps average -> recommend 2x 80GB GPU nodes + 1 warm spare for redundancy for Candidate A.
- Peak (1-minute bursts to ~35 concurrent): allow autoscale headroom to 3–4 nodes; autoscale policy with 2–3 minute cooldown.
- Cost sensitivity: switching from 70B to 13B reduces per-token GPU time by ~2.5–3x in typical short-query patterns, and batching can recover some of that for 70B on summarization tasks.

3) Latency / quality tradeoffs:
- For P95 latency target ~350ms on UI Q&A, Candidate A fits better with smaller batch sizes (1–4) and prefix cache for repeated queries.
- For summarization jobs that can be async, use Candidate B behind an async queue with larger batch sizes to improve throughput.

4) Canary suggestion: route 5% of traffic to Candidate B for summarization endpoints and monitor quality regressions using your eval prompt set; if no regression for 7 days, ramp to 25%.

Related: I uploaded a short shared doc with the canary checklist: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1XyZ-demo-model-shortlist

Happy to map this into a Dedicated node recommendation once we have exact RPS/time-of-day curves from your sheet. Can we schedule a 30-minute technical sync tomorrow or Wednesday to lock down router rules and fallback policies?
